overall_summary: First-person speculative hazard hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') focusing on extreme exoplanets and cosmic anomalies consistently generate the highest baseline views (800-1,050+ views) and strongest engagement (up to 3.7% like ratio). Conversely, recycled low-stakes psychology facts and repeated stock biology trivia stagnate below 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-person hazard hypothetical with sensory planetary extremes
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,028 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) dramatically outperform general statements.
winning_patterns.action: Frame high-concept astronomy and extreme physics through direct 'What If You Fell Into / Landed On...' visceral survival perspectives.

winning_patterns.pattern: Mind-bending cosmic paradoxes with clear numerical/physical contrast
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (980 views, 21 likes) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,027 views, 36 likes) drive rapid traction compared to abstract trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Lead with visual contradictions (e.g. atmospheric temperatures hot enough to rip molecules apart) in the first 2 seconds.

weak_patterns.pattern: Repeated generic psychology trivia without narrative stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' uploaded across multiple variations yielded 5 to 53 views; earworm trivia averaged under 50 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt generic psychology uploads unless framed as an immersive psychological test or micro-mystery with immediate viewer involvement.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple uploads of 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' plateaued between 118 and 363 views with zero comment engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate textbook trivia; pivot animal content strictly to cinematic survival mechanisms or extreme deep-sea cryptid-like biology.
